summary: In December 2009 Environment Minister Jairam Ramesh announced in Parliament that India would cut the emission intensity of its GDP by 20-25 per cent by 2020 from 2005 levels; India's official reporting states that emission intensity fell by 24 per cent between 2005 and 2016.

govt_response.title: Climate change in India - mitigation (Biennial Update Report summary)
govt_response.summary: India's Biennial Update Report states emission intensity of GDP fell 24 per cent between 2005 and 2016, putting India on track to meet its voluntary 20-25 per cent target.

analysis:
Jairam Ramesh announced India's voluntary target in Parliament on 3 December 2009: a 20-25 per cent reduction in the emission intensity of GDP by 2020 relative to 2005, to be pursued without a legally binding cap.

India's Biennial Update Report to the UNFCCC, released in 2018, reports a 24 per cent reduction in emission intensity of GDP between 2005 and 2016. Independent summaries describe India as on track for the 20-25 per cent target.

The announced target is assessed as met.
notes: The 24 per cent figure is taken from the summary of India's Biennial Update Report on the Wikipedia 'Climate change in India' page; the primary BUR PDF was not opened. The Hindu, Business Standard and Indian Express URLs were seen in search results; the Wikipedia page was read.
